clue.text: P. Rubens at his disposal, held them

definitions.text: P. Rubens at his disposal, held them

indicators.note: disposal suggests arranging or laying out afresh, so the letters before it are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The painter Rubens kept these tools always to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposal' rearranges P, RUBENS, AT and HIS; the whole clue then describes what a painter like Rubens held.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubens was a painter, and a painter's hand-held tools are brushes for applying pigment.

clue.text: Country girl from Reading!

parts.note: Peru is a South American country
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally or Sarah

explanation.surface: A village lass hails from the Berkshire town of Reading.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R disguises 'Reading' as the town in Berkshire; it is the ordinary noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading through of a text.

clue.text: Medicines unopened-ailments appear

indicators.note: with no opening, the first letter of the word for medicines is lost

parts.note: pills are medicines taken by mouth

explanation.surface: When the medicine bottles stay sealed, sicknesses show up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ills are troubles of body or health, much like disorders.

clue.text: Drunkard to pitch on top of grass

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to pitch a coin is to toss it
grass is slang for cannabis, also called pot

explanation.surface: A drunk is told to throw something onto the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A tosspot is an old word for a heavy drinker or sot.

clue.text: Letter from America?

parts.note: reads as a postal letter or the famous radio series, but means one who lets property, in US usage

explanation.surface: A correspondent sends news home from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' is one who lets, a landlord's agent; in America an estate agent is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English an estate agent who arranges property sales and lettings has this title.

clue.text: Littoral, they say, this play wright

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than seen, so the word for littoral is pronounced

parts.note: the littoral is the coast or shore

explanation.surface: Coastal scenes, people report, suit this dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the word for coast is pronounced the same as the dramatist's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish dramatist, a famous writer of stage works.

clue.text: You or I spoken as one?

definitions.text: You or I spoken as one?

parts.words: You or I spoken as one?
parts.note: the letter U said out loud sounds like the pronoun, and U (uranium) or I (iodine) is a chemical symbol

explanation.surface: A grammar question about which pronoun to say.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the symbol for uranium and I for iodine; 'you' is how U is said.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranium and iodine are each a chemical substance listed in the periodic table.

clue.text: Taking off soprano in time, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps marks the letters of the preceding words as one possible arrangement among others

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer leaves the stage right on cue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SOPRANO IN TIME; 'Taking off' looks like departure but means mimicking.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking off someone is mimicking them, an imitation of their voice or manner.

clue.text: Across: Read letters-and substitute with others?

parts.note: trans- is a prefix meaning across, as in transatlantic
well-read people are literate

explanation.surface: A crossword-style instruction to read some letters and swap them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across' looks like a grid direction but is the prefix; 'Read' means educated.
explanation.definitionFit: To render text in another alphabet is to replace each written character with its counterpart.

clue.text: Game at which Elgin was champion!

definitions.text: Game at which Elgin was champion!

parts.words: Game at which Elgin was champion!
parts.note: a children's game played with glass balls, and Lord Elgin famously acquired the Parthenon sculptures named after him

explanation.surface: A man called Elgin won a playground tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Elgin carried off the Parthenon sculptures now in the British Museum, so he 'won' the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's game is played with small glass balls, and the Parthenon sculptures bear Elgin's name.

clue.text: Status of an RU team in a scrummage

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A

indicators.note: a rugby scrum mixes bodies up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Rugby Union side's standing, decided in a scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is Rugby Union, which long kept players unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpaid player has a non-professional standing, as Rugby Union players once did.

clue.text: A piece of cake that is light

definitions.meaning: an idiom for a simple task

explanation.definitionFit: Both a simple task and undemanding work are effortless.

clue.text: Picks out places to visit

explanation.definitionFit: To pick out is to notice, and tourist sites are locations worth seeing.

clue.text: One in study who heads chapter

indicators.note: in places the letter for one within the word for study

parts.note: a den is a private study
A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A scholar in his room presides over a book chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: A cathedral's chapter is its body of clergy, presided over by this cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a cathedral chapter is its senior clergyman.

clue.text: Cooking-pot from the southern states

explanation.definitionFit: An army camp kettle and a nickname for the American South share the name.

clue.text: Climb Every Mountain from The Sound of Music?

definitions.text: Climb Every Mountain from The Sound of Music?

parts.words: Climb Every Mountain from The Sound of Music?
parts.note: the musical's song title suggests ascending, and a run of notes climbs too

explanation.surface: A famous song from a Rodgers and Hammerstein musical.
explanation.walkthrough: To climb a mountain is to ascend it, and a run of musical notes such as do-re-mi climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb is to ascend, and a run of musical notes goes up step by step.

clue.text: Virtuoso player standing alone…

parts.note: a performer who plays a solo, alone at the front

explanation.surface: A star musician takes the stage without accompaniment.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer playing a solo part is alone, often a virtuoso in front of an orchestra.

clue.text: … in this, a detailed account

definitions.meaning: following the previous clue, a solo performance is where the player stands alone

explanation.definitionFit: A solo concert performance and a full narration of facts share the word.

clue.text: Compound for journey in the dark, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the phrase for the journey is pronounced

parts.note: a night ride is a journey after dark

explanation.surface: A chemist mentions a trip taken at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitride is a chemical compound of nitrogen with another element.

clue.text: Plays with the rate of exchange

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: exchange suggests swapping places, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler bets on the currency exchange rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rate of exchange' reads as currency; 'of exchange' rearranges THE RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama, the staging of works, is collectively called this.

clue.text: Celebrated with tangled net around pit

indicators.note: around puts the jumbled net letters either side of the word for pit
a tangled net is jumbled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Something famous caught in a knotted net round a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pit' reads as a hollow, but here it is a coal working; 'tangled' rearranges the net, and 'around' wraps it about the pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone distinguished or renowned is famous and highly regarded.

clue.text: Unusual place to find this smelly creature

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters set out in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange spot to come across a stinking animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This European mammal of the weasel family is known for its foul smell.

clue.text: President tending to be easily led

parts.note: liable to means apt or tending to be

explanation.surface: A president who is inclined to be a pushover.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone flexible and readily influenced is supple in mind.

clue.text: Dog-end cut short

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
the tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: A cigarette butt trimmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog-end' is British slang for a cigarette butt, here split into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail is to reduce or truncate something.

clue.text: Heaps of sand, of course, in the river

definitions.meaning: on a golf course, players once teed off from small heaps of sand

explanation.definitionFit: Golf's starting mounds and a north-east English river share the name; the Tees flows through Middlesbrough.

clue.text: Note which can be read backwards

indicators.note: a word that reads the same in both directions is all the wordplay

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A musical note that reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A half note in music, worth two crotchets, is a minim.

clue.text: Title of a rabbit in a sombrero?

indicators.note: in marks letters sitting inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A rabbit wearing a Mexican hat, and what to call him.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Uncle Remus stories, Brer is the title of Rabbit and Fox, meaning brother.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Uncle Remus folk tales the rabbit is addressed with this dialect form of brother.

clue.text: Original cast of "My Fair Lady" without tea in this festival

indicators.note: without means the word for tea is taken away

parts.note: My Fair Lady is based on Pygmalion, whose sculptor's statue in myth was named Galatea
taken as written

explanation.surface: The first-night actors of a musical skip tea at a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original cast' is the statue Pygmalion carved, the origin of the musical's story.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive celebration or special entertainment.

clue.text: Penny gets into such a hole!

definitions.text: Penny gets into such a hole!

parts.words: Penny gets into such a hole!
parts.note: a coin is fed into a narrow opening in a machine, though Penny sounds like a girl in trouble

explanation.surface: A girl called Penny lands herself in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins go into a narrow opening on a vending machine.

clue.text: Gross insult-new route is lined with silver

indicators.note: lined with puts the silver symbol inside the rearranged route
new signals the word route being remade in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An offensive remark about a new road with a silver lining.
explanation.definitionFit: An affront or atrocity provokes fierce indignation.

clue.text: Coarse aggregate of political party returned, finally

indicators.note: returned means the party's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour party
last means finally

explanation.surface: A heap of political junk, the party finally come back.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballast is gravel or crushed stone used as a base for railways and roads.

clue.text: Kind of store in which to go barmy?

parts.note: to go is to depart
barmy means mad, slang mental

explanation.surface: A shop where staff are going mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A department store sells many kinds of goods in separate sections.
